notes:
**Document (134-2.147.note.document).** Continuation of the letter, with author page number 2 and archive pencil foliation 147. No date, salutation or signature is on this sheet. Its final “Je te remercie” continues beyond the page. H’s editorial note already records both visible page numbers.

**Claims, proposal and questions (134-2.147.claim.desiderata).** The author criticises the absence of a definition of a functor from ens. (semi) simpliciaux to n-groupoïdes. He calls the geometric intuition clear and says a theory omitting the functor would seem “canularesque”. His proposed wish-list of notions and relations is expressly tentative: “Peut-être”, “voudrait disposer”, “arriverait-on”, and “à la rigueur” qualify the hope that an axiomatic description might produce an explicit construction or an existence-and-uniqueness theorem. The second paragraph says “n’ayant pas compris l’idée de Segal” and “je ne vois pas comment tu définis les n-cat. de Picard”, followed by “mais peu importe”; the letter containing that idea was sent to Illusie. For strict Picard n-categories, he asks for an inserted (n+1)-catégorie that is (n+1)-équivalente to complexes de chaines de longueur n, and asks “D’accord ?”. These are reported proposals and questions, not verified equivalences or existence claims.

**Reading decisions and limits (134-2.147.note.readings).** The readers independently inspected both n+1 expressions, their plus signs and parentheses, the category qualifiers and final length n; mathematical expectation supplied no missing ink. The final words dont on and qui are readable over their older layers, which remain tentatively qu’on and pour. The ending after écri remains ambiguous both in its cancelled letters vant and in whether re was separately rewritten. The irregular live sequence “qui, soit donne/donner … soit qui permette” is preserved, with donne/donner unresolved. The pronoun is qu’ils, without a grammatical repair to elles. A raised apostrophe settles qu’une against the third reader’s que une. The initial barred m is resolved. Both sets of quotation marks are paired high strokes. Two faint points after Comme and a low comma-like mark after longueur remain explicitly uncertain; copying traces are possible. No proof, independent re-proof or mathematical computation was performed.
